title: CS170: Efficient Algorithms and Intractable Problems

unit.title: Inversion Counting: From Algorithm to Reliable Component
prerequisites: Comfort with sequences, recursion, and asymptotic notation
Ability to write and run Python 3.11 code and unittest tests
Mathematical maturity comparable to CS61B and CS70
learning_objectives: Turn a mathematical definition into a precise, side-effect-aware API contract
Design and justify a worst-case O(n log n) inversion-counting algorithm
Implement a deterministic command-line component with explicit failure behavior
Use examples, a small reference oracle, seeded generation, and subprocess checks to test behavior
Collect reproducible timing evidence without treating a benchmark as a proof of complexity
Communicate invariants, correctness, complexity, and engineering tradeoffs concisely

unit_completion_requires: All required artifacts are present and learner-authored
The implementation and documented commands run in the declared environment
Harness-controlled validation confirms functional, complexity, isolation, and interface requirements
The design note and comprehension responses provide reviewable reasoning
Benchmark evidence includes reproducibility metadata and is labeled as empirical evidence
